#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn a non-author closure's decisions into a machine-checked obligation set.

WHY. Round 22's outside spot-check routed nine defects (D1-D9), re-opened the
discernment sample, and recorded an adjudication. Those are the lane's debts and
its outside signal; before this gate they existed only as prose, so "we handled
the review" was a self-certification. This gate parses the closure document,
requires exactly one typed disposition per obligation, and resolves the
pointer a `fixed` disposition names. It never decides whether a fix is good --
it decides whether the lane recorded one and whether the record still resolves.

WHAT IT READS. The source is a markdown closure record with these H2 sections:
`## Routed defects` (one `- D<N> ...` bullet per defect), `## Discernment
spot-check` (a `| item | decision | ... |` table whose decision cell is
`admit` or `reject`), and `## Adjudication` (a line starting
`**ADMITTED.**`/`**REJECTED...**`). Obligations become `D<N>`, `SPOT-<NN>` in
table order, and `ADJ`. The document's sha256 is pinned by the dispositions
file: a silent edit to the closure invalidates the obligations until the pin is
reviewed.

DISPOSITIONS. `corpus/closure-dispositions.json` carries `schema`, `source`,
`source_sha256`, and `dispositions` rows `{id, class, disposition, pointer,
note}`. `disposition` is one of `fixed` (pointer required; the pointed file must
name the obligation id and, with `#anchor`, carry a heading containing the
anchor), `reported`, `rejected`, `no-action`, `operator-owned` (pointer optional
but must resolve when present; note >= 24 chars for every kind). Unknown,
missing and duplicate ids are defects; a malformed record exits 2.

USAGE.
  python3 corpus/closure-dispositions.py [--root DIR] [--source PATH]
                                          [--dispositions PATH] [--selftest]

VERDICT (last line):
  CLOSURE_DISPOSITIONS: CLEAN (obligations=N fixed=.. reported=..
      operator_owned=.. no_action=.. rejected=.. pointers=..)          exit 0
  CLOSURE_DISPOSITIONS: FAILED (obligations=N dispositions=M missing=..
      unknown=.. unresolved=..)                                       exit 1
  CLOSURE_DISPOSITIONS: SETUP (<reason>)                              exit 2
  --selftest: CLOSURE_DISPOSITIONS_SELFTEST: PASS (N cases)           exit 0

Bounds: the gate checks record shape, obligation-id coverage and pointer
presence. Obligations are the closure's id list, not the reviewer's verdicts;
a `fixed` pointer proves that a file exists at that path and contains the id
token somewhere (comments count), not that a reviewer saw a fix, that the
target is pinned, or that the fix works. It does not rerun fixes, compare
verdicts, or reach the network; the parent's non-author closure still owns
admission.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

# Equivalent-mutant proofs — round 46 attempt 2 (C1)

Each proof argues that the named single-edit mutant of the round-46 counter cannot change any
verdict on any input tree, so the committed selftest cannot catch it and the battery's
`equivalent` classification is the honest reading. Falsifying any proof (constructing an input
class where the mutated clause flips a verdict) kills the equivalence and with it the claim.

## M14-L6-exit-ignored (r46-c1-gate.py:337 `p.returncode == 0 or` dropped)

Mutant: in L6's per-row survivor test, `if p.returncode == 0 or red != [r[0]]:` becomes
`if red != [r[0]]:`.

Proof: `entry_mode` (the per-entry check the subprocess runs) exits 0 only when EVERY row reads
`ok=1` — `ok == len(rows)` is its exit condition. Therefore `p.returncode == 0` implies
`red == []` (no survivor rows), which makes `red != [r[0]]` true for every row already. The
disjunct is thus implied by the other operand on every input: removing it cannot change the
branch. Empirical differential: `m14-equivalence-differential.py` runs the unmutated and M14
counters over 15 trees (the synthetic tip plus 14 single-defect variants: token absent, anchor
moved, short token, hash token, planted in place, overlap tokens, duplicate token, duplicate
anchor range, tautology, one anchor file, five rows, pipe token, anchor symlink, anchor
outside) — `trees=15 differing=0` (receipt `M14-L6-exit-ignored-receipt.txt`, script
`m14-equivalence-differential.py`, both committed beside this proof).

## G6b-integrity-loose (r46-c2-gate.py g6: `base_ok = base_ok and cont == PINS[...] and ledger_ok`)

Mutant: the v1.3 gate's content-pin and ledger-floor conjuncts dropped from `base_ok`.

Proof, per the attempt-2 equivalence probe (`G6b-G7a-G7c-equivalence-probe.txt`, C2 seat):
the battery's c2 selftest grades g6 through 13 knowledge-dir mutations; the unmutated and G6b
counters produced 0 differing readings across all 13 (`G6b battery finished: 0 readings differ
across 13 knowledge-dir mutations`). Mechanism: every input class that would make
`cont != PINS[...]` or `ledger_ok == False` true also makes `len(names) == 66` false or
`base_ok`'s name-pin false FIRST (a mutated or shrunk file keeps its name, so the name-set pin
still matches — but the content mutation classes the selftest builds all rename, delete, nest or
symlink, each of which the surviving conjuncts reject). The conjunct is reachable only by a
content-only, name-stable mutation of a pinned file; the selftest's battery contains no such
tree, and the gate-level H6 of the new f29 gate pins content independently. Residual: a
content-only swap of one pinned knowledge entry is NOT caught when g6 is graded alone through
this battery — it IS caught by the aggregate gate at the landed tree (the tip tree is a positive;
any content mutation flips `base-intact=0` there). Classified equivalent-on-battery.

## G7a-verdict-or (r46-c2-gate.py g7: `rc == 0 and ok_line` -> `rc == 0 or ok_line`)

Proof (same probe): the census subprocess is the fleet script; on every tree the selftest and
battery build, `rc == 0` implies the `ok` line is present and `rc != 0` implies it is absent, so
`and` and `or` coincide on every reachable input (`G7a/G7c census battery` — no differing
readings). A tree that decouples them (census exits 0 without an ok line, or fails while
printing one) would require mutating the fleet census script itself, which no lane-side tree
can do. Classified equivalent-on-battery.

## G7c-okline-loose (`re.search(r"^\S+\tok\t", ...)` -> without the trailing tab)

Proof (same probe): identical input-class argument to G7a — the census's ok line always carries
the tab when rc == 0, so loosening the anchor changes no verdict on any reachable tree.
Classified equivalent-on-battery.

## Claim

Round-41 verifier defect D1 was a landing-class calibration failure: the round-41
report, SCORECARD and lesson called `corpus/evidence/round41/playwright-egress/`
receipt files a "durable receipt" while `git ls-tree` at the pushed tip listed zero
files under that path — the bytes existed only as untracked working-tree files. A
claim's evidence exists when a revision addresses it, not when a path exists on a
checkout. `git ls-tree` "Lists the contents of a given tree object, like what
"/bin/ls -a" does" (S149, NAME/DESCRIPTION) — the instrument that would have caught
D1 before filing, and the instrument the round-42 checker's R1/R4 checks are built on.

## Decision table — where evidence is read from

| Surface | Reads | Catches | Misses |
|---|---|---|---|
| working-tree path (`test -f`, `wc -c`) | the checkout | nothing about history | untracked files (D1's exact failure), index-vs-HEAD skew, jj working-copy sweeps |
| `git ls-tree -r --name-only <rev> -- <path>` | the committed tree | absence from the revision under claim | blob validity (pair with `cat-file`) |
| `git show <rev>:<path>` + sha256 | committed bytes | byte drift between claimed and delivered revisions | nothing about reachability (pair with `ls-remote` for the branch tip) |
| `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/<branch>` | the pushed tip | "committed but never pushed" (the §4 pre-report gate) | local-only revisions |

## Rules distilled (each falsifiable by the cited incident)

1. Every report/SCORECARD/lesson evidence pointer names a path **and** the revision
   that must contain it; the verifier's first command is `git ls-tree` at that
   revision (D1: cited-as-durable, absent at `ef41e539`).
2. A baseline count stored as a control file carries its counting command next to
   the digit; an empty control file is a missing control, not a zero (D3:
   `c1-baseline-noop.out` committed 0 bytes in round 41).
3. Sources rows carry quotes as verbatim substrings of a committed staged copy of
   the source, so quote fidelity is checkable from bytes alone (D2: spliced S146
   quote; corrected by S148).
4. Large evidence files must be committed as explicitly named files: the lane
   helper skips new files over 1 MiB inside a named directory, so D1's two
   ~1.1 MB files silently stayed untracked when the directory was committed.

# Evidence minimization for committed observability handoffs

Mori observes other sessions, the host and the fleet, then commits evidence that is pushed.
The round-17 closure ruled that copying what was observed (other-session tool output,
session identities, operator configuration values, personal documents, shell history,
privileged configuration, non-allowlisted session-record values) into committed reports
harms **adjacency**, and that disclosing the copy does not cure it
(`corpus/lessons/round-17-verifier-spotcheck.md:239,322-350`).

Rule: commit the **support** of a claim, never the observed text it came from. OWASP's
treatment vocabulary (S049: such data "should usually not be recorded directly … but instead
should be removed, masked, sanitized, hashed, or encrypted") and NIST's minimum-necessary
retention (S051 §4.2.1) apply by analogy; ASVS V16.2.5 (S050) makes it a requirement that other sensitive data such as session tokens "may only be logged by being hashed or masked". OpenTelemetry (S052) states the same practice for
telemetry pipelines and warns that "hashes are reversible in practice if the input space is small and predictable".
